summary: Steel lookout built 1941 on Spades Mountain, Idaho; moved to Long Mountain in 1963-64; sold and moved to Dave Kresek's land east of Spokane in 1998; NHLR-registered 1999.

facts.design: 50-foot Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab (NHLR); the earlier 1941 steel tower on Spades Mountain is given as 54 feet (FFLOS)

staffing.status: No staffing at the present site is described; the latest staffing in these sources is 1967 on Long Mountain, Idaho

access.note: On 30 acres of private property; the Register says visits are by prior appointment through the Fire Lookout Museum

visit.trail_note: Visits by prior appointment through the Fire Lookout Museum, per the Register; no public access is described

events.note: Steel tower erected on Spades Mountain, Kootenai County, Idaho; the Register and the FFLOS record both give 1941
Moved to Long Mountain, a station of the Idaho Dept. of Lands near Sandpoint. FFLOS and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the move 1963; the Register and the Forest Lookouts page say 1964
Joyce Sprinkle of Tucson began work as fire lookout on Long Mountain (Sandpoint News Bulletin, as quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)
Idaho Dept. of Lands offered the tower for sale with removal required by September 30, 1998; sold to Dave Kresek and moved to his private property
Registered November 20, 1999 as US 329, WA 35; nominated by Ray Kresek, Washington Registrar

corrections.why: The record starts at Long Mountain. Sources show a first site on Spades Mountain, and the 'None relocated' label contradicts the note that the tower was moved.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 1963; the Register and the Forest Lookouts page say 1964, which the Register ties to the Idaho Dept. of Lands taking it over. Both dates are kept and the story says so.

The Register gives 50 feet with a 7-by-7 metal cab; the 1964 Long Mountain listing gives 46 feet for an MC-40 steel tower; FFLOS and the 1998 sale notice give 54 feet, the sale notice with a 12-by-12 wood cabin. None is chosen as correct; the story gives all three. The height_m value is the Register's figure.

notes_for_editor: The record calls this the Long Mountain lookout, but the steel tower's first home was Spades Mountain (1941). A new Long Mountain station was nearing completion in 1959; the steel tower arrived in 1963 or 1964. Dates and heights disagree across sources and the story reports the disagreement. Only the NHLR page describes the present site; it says visits are by prior appointment through the Fire Lookout Museum, and nothing else about access was found. The FFLOS Spades Mountain page describes a separate 67-foot timber tower on that site, which is not the Kresek tower. The agency field 'Dave Kresek' matches the NHLR's administered-by line.
